description: SAKAN SPACE is a multidisciplinary team of engineering students, researchers, and innovators competing in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Combining expertise in Mechatronics, AI, Machine Learning, Data Analysis, and Software Development, we transform microgravity combustion data into innovative insights to advance fire safety research and support future human space exploration.
summary:
SAKAN SPACE is an offline-capable web application that organizes NASA microgravity-combustion research into a structured, source-cited knowledge base to support spacecraft fire-safety research.

The platform features three core modules: Mission Design Validator, Earth Spinoff & Research Hub, and Crisis Evidence Co-Pilot. It also includes a Search page and Ask SAKAN AI, with online AI integration through OpenRouter and an offline local AI fallback.

SAKAN promotes scientific transparency by labeling evidence as VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED, NOT REPORTED, or NOT AVAILABLE, while assessing source reliability and maintaining traceability.

It is a research and decision-support tool, not a certified safety system or an emergency-procedure source. It never declares any condition safe.
details:
SAKAN SPACE is an offline-capable research platform that organizes NASA microgravity-combustion research into a structured, traceable knowledge base containing 27 investigations and 88 scientific findings, each linked to source IDs and an evidence reliability score.

Evidence reliability is calculated using the OEC model: OEC = 0.30·SC + 0.20·DQ + 0.35·ES + 0.15·RR, with 19 High, 57 Moderate, 9 Low, and 3 Very Low findings.

The platform consists of three main modules:

01 — Mission Design Validator uses a 20-rule engine to assess mission-design conditions, calculate oxygen partial pressure (PO₂ = XO₂ × Ptotal), and generate evidence-backed assessments ranging from INSUFFICIENT DATA to HIGH RISK.

02 — Earth Spinoff & Research Hub provides an Arabic-English glossary of 84 scientific terms, interactive charts, research evolution, and Earth-based applications.

03 — Crisis Evidence Co-Pilot uses a weighted bilingual matching system to retrieve relevant published evidence for described scenarios, supported by voice input, text-to-speech, timers, and checklists. It identifies missing evidence without inventing emergency procedures.

SAKAN features two AI systems. SAKAN Local AI operates entirely in the browser without an internet connection, combining a bilingual BM25 retriever, trained intent classifier, rule engine, and numerical flame-behaviour models trained on ACME data. It is a specialized research system, not a generative LLM.

Online SAKAN AI, powered by OpenRouter language models through a FastAPI backend hosted on Replit, provides real-time AI assistance. In automatic mode, it explains scientific assessments and crisis evidence in the user's language, referencing verified findings and their evidence status. If the online backend becomes unavailable, the application automatically falls back to SAKAN Local AI.

Model evaluation using grouped, held-out 70/30 splits achieved 0.633 PSI router top-1 accuracy and 0.984 top-3 accuracy, 0.851 intent-classifier accuracy (template split), and 0.83 balanced accuracy for the self-extinguishing model. The burn-time model achieved an R² of 0.20, indicating limited predictive performance. Hot-ignition and cool-flame targets were excluded because the available data were unsuitable.

SAKAN prioritizes scientific transparency and safety. It distinguishes VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED, NOT REPORTED, and NOT AVAILABLE evidence, and never declares any condition safe. Its reliability scores reflect source quality, not physical safety.

The platform is not a certified safety system or an emergency-procedure source. Its findings are limited to publicly available research, online AI availability depends on free-tier services, and speech recognition depends on browser support.

Future development includes expanding the knowledge base as NASA publishes new investigations, improving numerical models as more consistent experimental data become available, and obtaining expert review of the validation rules.

Technology Stack: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Node.js, Python FastAPI, Vercel, Replit, and OpenRouter API.
